Chapter 05

The map: every feature, every library, and where it lives

A reference chapter. Every Svelte 5 and SvelteKit 3 feature the project uses, every ecosystem library it reaches for, and the chapter where each one is built and explained — so you can read the course in order or jump to the thing you came for.

By the end of this chapter

Know where to find everything, and see at a glance how much of a real product is the framework and how much is the ecosystem around it.

This is the table of contents by *feature* rather than by chapter. Come back to it whenever a term in a later chapter is unfamiliar: everything is listed with the chapter that builds it.

Glossary. Nine words the rest of the course uses without stopping, as SvelteKit’s glossary defines them. SSR, server-side rendering: the server produces the page’s HTML. CSR, client-side rendering: JavaScript in the browser produces or updates it. Hydration: the browser takes over server-rendered HTML, checks the DOM is what it expects and attaches the event listeners, using the data the server sent along rather than fetching it again. Hybrid: SvelteKit’s default — the first page by SSR, every later navigation by CSR. Prerendering: rendering a page once, at build time, and serving the saved HTML to everybody; possible when any two people asking get the same page. SSG, static site generation: a site where every page is prerendered. Edge: rendering in a content delivery network, near the person asking. ISR, incremental static regeneration: generating static pages on request, without a redeploy (an adapter-vercel feature). PWA, progressive web app: a web app that can be installed and behave like a native one, usually with a service worker for offline use. Meridian is hybrid, prerenders its guides, and is none of the last three.

Svelte 5

  • $state, $derived, $derived.by, $effect, $props — everywhere; the pattern that matters is TripState (ch. 26), a class whose fields are all derived from one getter.
  • Assignable $derived — the stop dialog’s fields start from the stop being edited and belong to the form after that (ch. 27).
  • untrack — reading a prop once, on purpose, in a component the page keys on its slug (ch. 26, 33).
  • $state.raw, $state.snapshot — the Tiptap editor instance (ch. 32); the library’s toJSON (ch. 07).
  • await in markup, in $derived and at the top of <script>; <svelte:boundary> with pending and failed — the trip page, the globe, the trips list, the explore page (ch. 26, 30, 35, 37).
  • {const} declaration tags, which replaced {@const}, bare and with $derived — {@const x = y} becomes {const x = $derived(y)}, and a bare {const} is the different, once-only thing; the header’s link list, the trip page’s initial data, the globe’s import (ch. 23, 25, 26, 30).
  • class={[…]} and class={{…}} — every conditional class, in place of the class: directive they replaced in Svelte 5.16 (ch. 25).
  • Attachments — {@attach}, and fromAction for a library that ships an action — Tiptap (ch. 32), the GSAP hero timeline, attached only when motion is wanted (ch. 23), svelte-dnd-action (ch. 27), the expenses table’s overflow (ch. 31), and the argument for when a wrapper library is *not* worth it (ch. 42).
  • animate:flip with svelte-dnd-action (ch. 27, 24).
  • Motion: transition:, in:, a custom TransitionConfig with css(t, u), svelte/easing, Tween from svelte/motion, prefersReducedMotion — the copy button’s check mark, the invite link, the map’s status pill, the tab indicator, and every built-in the design brief keeps out, each with its rule (ch. 24, 26).
  • svelte/reactivity: MediaQuery, createSubscriber; svelte/reactivity/window: scrollY, online — the theme, geolocation, the header, the trip header’s “Offline” (ch. 23, 29, 30, 43, 39).
  • Custom elements — customElement: true and the generated .element class, registered with customElements.define, with a shadow root and attribute-mapped props (ch. 38).
  • Runes in a .svelte.ts file inside a published library — the Route class (ch. 07).

SvelteKit 3

  • All configuration in vite.config.ts; preprocess, extensions, dynamicCompileOptions, the inspector passed through to vite-plugin-svelte, output.linkHeaderPreload; tsconfig.json extending $app/tsconfig (ch. 04).
  • src/env.ts with defineEnvVars, public, static (ch. 15).
  • Remote functions: query, query.batch, query.live, prerender, form, command; requested().refreshAll(); invalid() with issue.field(); getRequestEvent (ch. 17–20).
  • Hooks: handle with sequence, handleFetch, handleError with kind, init; the browser’s handleError; universal reroute and transport; hook types from @sveltejs/kit/hooks (ch. 15, 21, 22).
  • defineParams in src/params.ts (ch. 15), and the typed params a page receives through PageProps from ./$types (ch. 26).
  • Route groups and the layout split — (site) with identity, guides without (ch. 25, 36).
  • Prerendering with entries, csr = false, per-locale output through reroute (ch. 36).
  • resolve() from $app/paths with typed route ids, and paths.relative: false (ch. 25, 37).
  • tracing: { server: true } and src/instrumentation.server.ts (ch. 37).
  • CSP mode: "auto", csrf, version.pollInterval and updated.current, preload by source filename (ch. 04, 25, 47).
  • $app/env: browser, building, dev, version (ch. 25, 30, 26, 38).
  • onNavigate view transitions, beforeNavigate, afterNavigate (ch. 25, 39).
  • Shallow routing: goto('', { shallow: true, state }), page.state, App.PageState, history.back() — the stop dialog as a history entry (ch. 27).
  • snapshot() from $app/navigation — a half-typed new trip that survives a reload (ch. 35).
  • query.live authorised on every wake, with getRequestEvent() after a yield (ch. 19).
  • A service worker: src/service-worker/index.ts, self from $app/service-worker, immutable/assets/prerendered from $app/manifest, version as the cache name, $app/tsconfig/service-worker, automatic registration — the offline itinerary, and the copies a shared device forgets (ch. 39).
  • <enhanced:img> (ch. 23).
  • adapter-node with precompress, paths.origin, a health endpoint, graceful shutdown (ch. 48).

The toolchain

  • sv create, sv add, sv check — the scaffold line that reproduces this project’s tooling, what each add-on writes, and community add-ons (ch. 03).
  • svelte-check with --fail-on-warnings, and every other flag it takes (ch. 03).
  • ESLint and Prettier — projectService for .svelte and .svelte.ts, eslint-config-prettier, .prettierignore as the map of generated folders (ch. 03).
  • The Svelte AI tools — AGENTS.md, the MCP server, the skills, the svelte-file-editor subagent, the Claude Code plugin, and lint:svelte, the autofixer over every component in verify (ch. 03).
  • The workspace — pnpm 12, allowBuilds, a minimum release age, .vscode/extensions.json (ch. 02).
  • Diagnostics by code — compiler warnings and errors, runtime errors and warnings, zero svelte-ignore, and the autofixer as a gate (ch. 45).
  • sv migrate — task-based migrations, one task per commit, MIGRATION_TASKS.md resolved into docs/migration-sveltekit-3.md, and the Svelte 4 legacy table (ch. 49).
  • The exit criteria — every planned surface, taught, declined, deferred or dropped, generated and checked (ch. 51).

The ecosystem

Each library, what it is for here, its shape, and the chapter. The survey in chapter 40 is where the alternatives are weighed; this is just the roll-call.

  • Bits UI 2 — Dialog, Combobox, Command, DateRangePicker, DatePicker. Headless. (ch. 22, 27, 28, 31, 35, 41)
  • svelte-maplibre 2 + MapLibre GL 6 — the map. Wrapper. (ch. 29, 42)
  • Threlte 8 (@threlte/core, @threlte/extras) + three.js — the globe. Wrapper. (ch. 30, 42)
  • svelte-dnd-action — dragging stops between days. An action, applied through fromAction. (ch. 27)
  • TanStack Table v9 (@tanstack/svelte-table) — the expenses table. Headless. (ch. 31, 41)
  • LayerChart 2 — two charts. Components over d3 scales. (ch. 31)
  • Tiptap 3 (@tiptap/core, @tiptap/starter-kit, @tiptap/extension-placeholder) — the notes editor, and the sentence it shows while empty. Imperative, through an attachment. (ch. 32, 41)
  • Paraglide 2 (@inlang/paraglide-js) — three languages. Compiler + Vite plugin. (ch. 21)
  • Better Auth 1.7 (better-auth/minimal) — accounts and sessions. Server library with a SvelteKit handler. (ch. 16, 34)
  • Drizzle ORM + libSQL — the database. (ch. 14)
  • valibot — every schema, from forms to environment variables to frontmatter. (ch. 13)
  • svelte-sonner — toasts. (ch. 23)
  • phosphor-svelte — icons, with the Vite plugin that keeps the dev server fast. (ch. 04, 23)
  • runed — Debounced on the explore page, and the argument about when a utility library is worth it. (ch. 37, 43)
  • mdsvex — the guides. Preprocessor. (ch. 36)
  • @sveltejs/enhanced-img — the hero. Preprocessor. (ch. 23)
  • @sveltejs/package, publint, @arethetypeswrong/cli — packaging the library. (ch. 09)
  • @internationalized/date — calendar dates without time zones, and the transport hook that carries them (ch. 22).
  • world-atlas + topojson-client — the coastlines, at build time. (ch. 17, 29)
  • @opentelemetry/sdk-trace-node — the tracing exporter. (ch. 37)
  • GSAP — one hero timeline, respecting reduced motion. (ch. 23)
  • fontsource — two variable fonts, preloaded by source filename. (ch. 23)
  • axe-core + @axe-core/playwright — every WCAG 2 A and AA rule over every screen, in both themes, as part of the end-to-end suite. Dev only. (ch. 46)
  • sv + @sveltejs/mcp — the Svelte CLI and the Svelte AI tools, locked by pnpm-lock.yaml so everybody runs the same versions. Dev only. (ch. 03)

The domain, with no framework in it

  • Geodesy — haversine distance, bearings, great-circle interpolation, unwrapped arcs, bounds, compass points, Intl distance formatting. (ch. 06)
  • Ids, dates, money — unguessable slugs; ISO dates with cached Intl formatters; integer minor units with fractionDigits asked of Intl. (ch. 10)
  • Fair splits — shares by largest remainder, balances, greedy settlement. (ch. 11)
  • The itinerary — grouping by day, placing a stop, renumbering only what moved. (ch. 12)
  • Schemas and roles — one valibot schema per input; who may do what. (ch. 13)

Proving and shipping

  • Vitest, two projects — pure logic in Node; components in Chromium with vitest-browser-svelte. (ch. 44)
  • Playwright — seven suites on a desktop and a Pixel 7, including two browser contexts on one trip, and the design’s checks at 360px as well. (ch. 46)
  • Security — hooks, headers, CSP, CSRF, the one frameable route. (ch. 47)
  • Docker, compose, CI — three stages, a health check, SIGTERM, a workflow with verify, package, image and course jobs. (ch. 48)

Checkpoint

You do not need to remember this chapter. You need to know it exists, and to come back to it when a later chapter names something you have not met yet.
